findings_qualitative.value: CS, H2S, and H2CO show broken ring morphologies surrounding central absorption and peak at similar deprojected radial distances (~105-111 au), showing no radial chemical segregation within the beam resolution.

evidence.quote: CS and H$\rm _2$CO peak at the same position (0.75$\ensuremath{''}$, $\sim$ 105 au), while H$\rm _2$S peaks slightly farther out (0.8$\ensuremath{''}$, $\sim$ 111 au).
Accordingly, we observed no hints of chemical segregation in the radial direction within the angular resolution of our observations.

findings_qualitative.value: SO2 is only detected in emission on the western/southwestern side of the disk and along the streamer filament, with no central absorption.

evidence.quote: Three species, H$\rm _2$S, CS, and H$\rm _2CO$, are detected at all azimuths, while SO$\rm _2$ is only detected at the southwestern side of the disk.

claims.hypothesis: Comparing molecular column density ratios between the envelope and protoplanetary disk of HL Tau reveals whether gas is chemically reprocessed from the envelope to the disk.
claims.experiment: Derive column densities and ratios of CS, H2S, and H2CO in the absorbing envelope and emitting protoplanetary disk using NOEMA observations.
claims.result: The N(CS)/N(H2S) ratio is 23 to 70 times (40 to 50 times in abstract/summary) larger in the envelope than in the disk.
claims.finding: Significant differences in molecular ratios between the envelope and disk indicate chemical reprocessing/evolution during the transition from envelope to protoplanetary disk, and N(CS)/N(H2S) can differentiate envelope from disk emission.

evidence.loc: Column densities and molecular ratios: Envelope versus disk
evidence.quote: The most notable difference is in the N(CS)/N(H$\rm _2$S) ratio, which is between 23 and 70 times larger in the envelope. This suggests chemical evolution in the transition from the envelope to the disk.
The most prominent difference is in the N(CS)/N(H$\rm _2$S) ratio, which is 40 to 50 times larger in the envelope.

claims.hypothesis: Localized SO2 emission and azimuthal chemical variations in the HL Tau disk are linked to the impact of a large-scale infalling streamer.
claims.experiment: Map four SO2 transitions with NOEMA, combine with ALMA detections from Garufi et al. (2022) in a rotational diagram, and compare N(H2S)/N(H2CO) across disk emission peaks.
claims.result: SO2 is detected only on the western side where the streamer impacts the disk with T_rot = 56 +/- 5 K and N(SO2) = (3.0 +/- 0.3)e14 cm^-2, and N(H2S)/N(H2CO) varies by almost a factor of five between the H2S and H2CO peaks.
claims.finding: SO2 emission likely traces gas sputtered/desorbed from dust grains by shocks where the streamer impacts the disk, while azimuthal variations in molecular ratios reflect localized streamer impact and differing turbulence.

evidence.quote: The most prominent difference is that of the N(H$\rm _2$S)/N(H$\rm _2$CO) ratio, which at 40 K is almost five times larger at the H$\rm _2$S peak compared to the H$\rm _2$CO peak.
The impact of the streamer in the disk results in a local enhancement of molecular species (including SO$\rm _2$) that are sputtered from the surface of dust grains in the protoplanetary disk.

why_this_data.value: HL Tau shows deep molecular absorption lines from its infalling envelope alongside disk emission, allowing direct comparison of column densities in the envelope and disk.

evidence.loc: Observations of sulfuretted species in HL Tau
evidence.quote: The source we focus on is HL Tau, where molecular absorption lines from the envelope have been detected, thus allowing for the derivation of column densities and molecular abundances.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thermal desorption as the origin of SO2 emission was rejected because it would produce azimuthally symmetric emission rather than localized western emission.

evidence.quote: As pointed out by (cite: Garufi2022), thermal desorption would result in an azimuthally symmetrical emission, rather than a localized emission.

limitations_admitted.value: SO2 column densities are lower limits because optically thick SO2 emission lines cannot be ruled out.

evidence.quote: Since we cannot rule out optically thick SO$\rm _2$ emission lines, the column densities reported here are lower limits.

limitations_admitted.value: Only one transition per molecule (CS, H2S, H2CO) was observed, requiring LTE and optically thin assumptions for disk column densities.

evidence.quote: We only have one transition per molecule, so we assumed local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE) and optically thin emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust optical depth at 2 mm (tau ~ 1) could cause continuum oversubtraction if line emission originates in colder regions like the midplane, making disk column densities lower limits.

evidence.quote: However, if the emission originates in a region with lower temperatures, such as the mid-plane, over-subtraction could be an issue. In any case, the reported column densities act as lower limits.

referee_caveats_inferred: Envelope column densities are measured along a single line of sight toward the central continuum absorption peak, whereas disk column densities are measured at outer ring peaks (~105 au), so the comparison probes different physical radii as well as different components.
Single-transition disk column densities rely on assumed uniform excitation temperatures (20, 40, 58 K) across all three molecules.
